candidates.title: replace_memory_range on a machine that shares its directory leaves the directory's unhashed config.json naming the old range, so after destroy + sync_stored the O2-guaranteed directory reloads to a state the machine never had (pre-replacement range spliced with post-run registers/buffers)
candidates.component: Emulator core: machine::replace_memory_range with sharing_mode::all (or a shared range under config) loads, and the persistence that sharing provides (machine destructor, sync_stored, reload); also the cartesi-machine CLI --load=<dir>,sharing:all[,sync] with --replace-memory-range
candidates.role: Sharing, syncing and loading machines: Honest operator (AUDIT.md table). replace_memory_range: rest of the machine API, off the PRT honest operator's path (inputs go through cmio). CLI: Support.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::replace_memory_range (~723-764: updates only the in-memory m_c and m_ars, never the directory's config.json nor m_initial_c, and does not refuse machines with shared backing stores); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp machine_address_ranges::replace (~656-683: refuses only protected / host-read-only ranges); src/machine.cpp sync_stored (~712) and for_each_stored_filename (list files from the directory's on-disk config.json); src/cm.h cm_replace_memory_range doc (only says 'A later cm_store() uses the new backing store'); src/cartesi-machine.lua 2944-2956 (refuses replace only with --revert-mode=stored) and 4926-4938 (load_sync: destroy, sync_stored(load_dir), and for a remote machine load(load_dir) again).
candidates.description: A machine loaded with SHARING_ALL from directory D keeps every range mapped shared to D's files, and D's config.json (outside the hashed state) tells every later load which file backs each range. machine::replace_memory_range swaps a range's backing store in memory only: m_c and m_ars point to the replacement, but D's config.json still names D's old file for that range, and the old file stops receiving the guest's writes. Every other range keeps writing to D. The API neither refuses this on a machine with shared backing storage nor rewrites D. After the caller destroys the machine without a crash and runs sync_stored(D), D satisfies O2's definition of a guaranteed directory ('synced after the last change to its contents and ... destroyed without a crash before that sync'), yet it no longer holds the machine's state: it holds the pre-replacement contents of the replaced range together with the post-run processor state, tx buffer and other ranges. Reloading D, with or without clear_hash_tree, gives a root hash that is none of the machine's roots: a combination that no execution reaches. D's cached hash tree is consistent with D's contents, so verify_hash_tree and an O1 rebuild both pass and nothing detects the split. clone_stored(D) copies the same split state. With a shared replacement file outside D, sync_stored(D) also never syncs the file that holds the replaced range's current data. The CLI shows the developers know replacements do not survive a reload of the directory: it refuses --replace-memory-range with --revert-mode=stored. But it still accepts --load=D,sharing:all[,sync] --replace-memory-range with --revert-mode=none. With --remote-address and sync, the CLI destroys the remote machine, syncs D and loads D again, so the remote machine silently continues from the split state.
candidates.trigger: The trusted caller of the machine API (or the CLI user) loads a stored machine with SHARING_ALL, or with SHARING_CONFIG and that range marked shared, and calls replace_memory_range, for example to instantiate a template's input or output drive as the manual shows. It then runs the machine and persists it the way sharing documents: destroy (or process exit after destroy), sync_stored, and later load, clone or resume from D. No adversary or guest action is needed. Any guest run after the replacement makes the split visible.
candidates.reachability: Documented API calls on any valid template (the test uses the harness baremetal-template, a valid template). The replacement and the input delivery are ordinary operations. No unreachable state is involved, and the directory is one that O2 guarantees: the machine was destroyed without a crash before the sync, and the directory was not loaded with sharing again.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Checked exclusions. (a) 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented': the change itself (the live machine now has the replacement) works as documented. The defect is that persisting a shared machine through destroy and sync drops the change, and splits later guest writes between two files. That is not the effect of the change, and cm_replace_memory_range only says 'A later cm_store() uses the new backing store'. (b) 'Defects that need the honest operator to reload a stored directory that O2 does not guarantee': no. The machine was 'destroyed without a crash before that sync' and the directory was 'synced after the last change to its contents' (O2). (c) How to rate step 1: 'A wrong hash after documented operations, destroying the machine, and a sync is not' out of scope. Alternative reading: Low, as 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller', if replacing a range of a machine that shares its directory counts as misuse. Nothing in cm.h or the manual says so, and the API does not refuse it. 2. Role: sharing, syncing and reloading are 'storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines' = Honest operator (AUDIT.md table, section 3 'play this role in every deployment'). replace_memory_range is 'the rest of the machine API', and the PRT honest operator does not plausibly call it, since inputs are delivered through cmio. The CLI path is Support. 3. High/Medium cases: Medium fits: 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)'. D, a stored directory the machine shares, ends inconsistent with the machine's contents. 4. Critical, under the reading where a production node replaces ranges in a machine that shares its directory (as older rollups nodes did with input drives) and resumes from that directory. R2: 'Every way of copying, persisting, restoring, or sharing a machine' must agree on the canonical hash. Here sharing+destroy+sync+reload gives a different hash at the same mcycle. Section 4 / O2: a directory that O2 guarantees must not 'later load as a different state', and O2 itself warns of 'a combination that no execution reaches' only for a stop, not after a clean destroy and sync. For the CLI alone: Support, Medium only if the CLI counts as a tool that computes claims, else Low. Preferred: Medium (emulator, off-path API operation). Deciding fact: whether any production validator node calls replace_memory_range on a machine loaded with sharing.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred: off-path machine API operation leaving a shared, O2-guaranteed directory inconsistent with the machine). Critical if a production node replaces ranges of a shared machine and resumes from its directory. Low if read as trusted-caller misuse.
candidates.threat_to_goal: An operator that persists its machine by sharing and syncing, which is the documented way to get a guaranteed directory without a store, gets a directory that reloads to a state no execution reaches. It then computes claims from a wrong state, and its honest claim is lost (completeness failure). Even off the PRT path it breaks R2's promise that every way of persisting or sharing a machine agrees, and the manual's promise that 'with config or all, <directory> holds a valid machine' after a clean exit.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARCACHE/replace_shared2.lua (lua5.4 with bugs/env.sh; argument = a scratch dir). It clones baremetal-template/machine to D, syncs it, and loads it with clear_hash_tree and SHARING_ALL (root 0x428a6bb8...ac75). It replaces .ram with a copy that differs in one byte at 0x80100000 (root 0x31da7bf4...fdb6), delivers one advance input and runs to the next yield (break reason 3, root 0x1657c499...c7a5). It then destroys the machine, runs sync_stored(D), and reloads D with clear_hash_tree: root 0xa159b1f3...7cef, '== NONE of the machine's states'. D has mcycle 3530295 (post-input) but the RAM byte at 0x80100000 is 0 (pre-replacement image). The simpler /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARCACHE/replace_shared.lua shows that, right after the replacement, a plain reload of D returns the pre-replacement root 0x428a... with verify_hash_tree=true, so nothing detects it.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: clone the harness baremetal-template to a temporary D, sync, load with SHARING_ALL (clear_hash_tree), replace .ram (by label) with a modified image, deliver one advance input and run to the yield, and record get_root_hash() = H. Destroy, run sync_stored(D), reload D with clear_hash_tree. Exit 0 if replace_memory_range raised an error (refusing machines with shared backing storage is an acceptable fix), or if D's rebuilt root equals H (persisting the replacement into D is the other fix). Otherwise exit 1. Deterministic. About 1 s and 200 MB of temporary disk.

candidates.title: Unhashed backing_store.mark_pages_dirty in an adopted template's config.json survives clear_hash_tree and is re-emitted by every store and clone, so every later reload of the operator's own snapshots rehashes the whole range
candidates.component: Emulator core: loading and storing machines (machine_config::load keeps mark_pages_dirty; machine::store writes m_c via machine_config::store; memory_address_range constructor marks every page dirty when it is set)
candidates.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md: storing, loading, cloning and syncing machines)
candidates.location: src/json-util.cpp:1804 (reads mark_pages_dirty from config.json); src/machine-config.cpp adjust_ar_backing_store_config (strips create/truncate, rewrites filenames, but keeps mark_pages_dirty); src/machine-address-ranges.cpp prepare_ar_backing_store (~158-162); src/memory-address-range.cpp:76 (marks all pages dirty); src/machine.cpp:520 (store writes m_c.store(dir)) and clone_stored (copies config.json verbatim).
candidates.description: Same pattern as R1-O1-2, through a different unhashed field. backing_store.mark_pages_dirty is not in the hashed state, and adjust_backing_stores does not strip it, unlike create and truncate. A template distributed with mark_pages_dirty=true for a large range (RAM or a flash drive) keeps it after the operator's O1 adoption with clear_hash_tree. Every machine:store (any sharing mode) and clone_stored then writes it into the operator's own snapshots. Each later load of those snapshots marks every page of the range dirty and rehashes the whole range at the next get_root_hash, even though their cached trees were written by the operator's own process (which R1 lets the operator trust). In stored-player designs that reload the epoch machine after every input commit (PRT player: stored_machine_pair_methods:commit, clone_loaded_directory, new_machine_pair_from_entry), this adds a full rehash of the range to every input and every pair built from a cache entry. The root hash stays correct.
candidates.trigger: Whoever distributes or relays the template edits config.json (unhashed) and sets mark_pages_dirty=true on large ranges. The honest operator adopts it as O1 requires and keeps working on its own snapshots.
candidates.reachability: The template contents stay a valid template, and the root hash after the rebuild matches. Only an unhashed config field is changed. No machine state is involved.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope: likely. 'Average-case performance that does not change the worst-case cost of any operation listed in R12'. The worst case of loading already includes a full rehash (an adoption with clear_hash_tree), and the cost stays linear in the bytes the load covers. Not the snapshot exclusion: the contents are a valid template, and section 8 says 'nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory'. That list does not include cost, so it does not apply directly either. 2. Role: Honest operator (loading and storing machines). 3. High: only if read under 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load ..., multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor'. But the trigger is neither the guest nor host load, and the per-load worst case is unchanged. 4. Critical: no rule is violated at the R12 level, because the cost stays bounded and linear. 5. Low: a distributor-controlled unhashed field that survives the O1 rebuild and slows every later reload of the operator's own snapshots (the same root cause as R1-O1-2, but bounded).
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Out of scope as average-case performance under the strict reading)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal: roots stay correct and costs stay linear. It shows that the O1 rebuild cleans only the cached trees and not the other unhashed, distributor-chosen fields of config.json, which keep shaping the honest operator's costs in every snapshot derived from the template. Any fix for R1-O1-2 that resets phtc_size on adoption should also reset mark_pages_dirty (and should not trust the rest of the template's config.json).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARCACHE/mpd.lua. It clones baremetal-template/machine, sets ram.backing_store.mark_pages_dirty=true in config.json, adopts with clear_hash_tree (root unchanged, 0x428a...ac75), stores with the default SHARING_ALL and syncs. The operator's snapshot config.json then has mark_pages_dirty=true. Three reloads with SHARING_ALL each rehash 16393 pages at get_root_hash (0.09-0.19 s for 64 MiB). Control /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARCACHE/mpd_ctl.lua (same machine without the flag): 264 misses on the first reload after the store, 0 after, about 0.001 s.
candidates.test_idea: Adopt a copy of baremetal-template whose config.json sets ram mark_pages_dirty=true with clear_hash_tree, store it to S and sync, reload S twice, and require get_hash_tree_stats().phtc.page_misses on the second reload to be at most a small bound (for example 1024 pages), or require S/config.json to have mark_pages_dirty=false.

not_covered: Considered and refuted by experiment: a SMALL distributor-chosen hash_tree.phtc_size (1, the other extreme of R1-O1-2) does not slow hash-tree updates. phtc_small.lua: 20 rounds x 3000 dirty pages rehashed in 0.36 s with phtc_size=1 vs 0.41 s with 4096 on this 4-CPU host, same roots. Not reported.

Enumerated config.json fields and their load-time use. processor/uarch registers, dtb bootargs/init/entrypoint: ignored on load (backing stores are never newly_created after adjust_backing_stores), re-emitted by store. iunrep: cross-checked with the shadow (R1-R2-1 family). ram/flash/nvram start, length, read_only and flash-vs-nvram: all bound by the hashed PMA table (init_pmas_contents memcmp, DID and W flags). Labels: validated, used only for replace_memory_range lookup. virtio: refused for reproducible machines. hash_function: changes the rebuilt root, so the on-chain comparison catches it. shared/create/truncate: stripped or overridden except under SHARING_CONFIG. phtc_size: R1-O1-2. mark_pages_dirty: candidate 2. Data files longer than the range are refused by mapped_memory, and shorter files are R2-DFSTORED-2.

Cached files: hash_tree::clear resets the phtc, marks every dpt node dirty, clears dense trees and zeroes sparse hashes. update_sparse_tree resyncs sparse leaves with dense roots, and phtc hits require entry root == dht page hash. So a stale sht, or a phtc mismatched with data, from store(SHARING_CONFIG) mixes was judged harmless (read, not run). The phtc constructor's check_metadata was not fuzzed (R1-O1-1 area).

create(config, runtime, dir, SHARING_ALL) or create_stored with a config taken from get_initial_config() of a machine adopted with clear_hash_tree: prepare_ar_backing_store_for_share or prepare_ar_backing_store copy and trust the template's original .dht/.dpt again unless the runtime config repeats clear_hash_tree. Read only, not tested, not reported. It is the documented reuse of supplied tree files (manual 3299-3310) and arguably a deliberate API choice. It is a further re-emission site of the R2-DFSTORED-1 pattern.

replace_memory_range with replacement .dht/.dpt files: documented trust (cm.h example, manual 'reuses the dirty-page flags'). Not reported. Not tested: replace_memory_range followed by store(SHARING_NONE/CONFIG).

JSON-RPC: fork is refused for any shared backing store (machine::has_shared_backing_store covers the sht/phtc too). The load default is SHARING_NONE. Store/clone handlers call the same core code. fork/rebind/swap carry no persisted data. No JSON-RPC-specific variant was found, and none was exercised with crafted directories.

PRT player epoch and checkpoint directories. load_epoch_checkpoint takes the epoch's geometry from the unhashed epoch.json (log2_mcycles_per_period) and never compares it with the factory geometry that crisium reads from the chain. A stale checkpoints/epoch-0, kept by the early return in store_first_epoch_checkpoint, from a run with another geometry would make the player build claims at the wrong period. Judged operator misconfiguration of its own records (support). Not reported, not tested.

The cartesi-machine CLI reads unhashed creation-time registers from get_initial_config() (htif iyield/iconsole in check_cmio_htif_config, progress terminator) instead of the hashed shadow registers. Diagnostics only. Not reported.
cartesi-machine-stored-hash prints the cached root without a rebuild. The manual documents that it does not check directories the operator did not produce. Not reported.

Not covered: the Windows/macOS clone and copy paths, reflink filesystems, rename_stored/remove_stored while a machine still maps the directory, sync_stored durability of a shared replacement file outside the directory (noted in candidate 1 but not tested), and a full PRT player run (forked or stored) on a template with crafted config.json fields.
